classification.difficultyReason: Complete cumulative frequencies, determine the middle observation positions, and map them back to scores. The hardest part requires recognising that the two middle observations lie at different scores and averaging them; earlier parts scaffold the method.

content.prompt: Find the median from these frequency tables.

answer.worked:
Cumulative frequencies: $2,5,6,12,17,19$.

$$\begin{align*}n&=2+3+1+6+5+2\\n&=19\\M_p&=\frac{19+1}{2}\\M_p&=10\end{align*}$$

The cumulative frequency is $6$ through score $4$ and $12$ through score $6$, so the 10th observation is $6$.

$$\text{Median}=6$$

Check: the final cumulative frequency and $\Sigma f$ are both $19$.

Cumulative frequencies: $1,5,17,26,38,47$.

$$\begin{align*}n&=1+4+12+9+12+9\\n&=47\\M_p&=\frac{47+1}{2}\\M_p&=24\end{align*}$$

The cumulative frequency is $17$ through $x=3$ and $26$ through $x=4$, so the 24th observation is $4$.

$$\text{Median}=4$$

Cumulative frequencies: $9,24,56,94,116,129,136$.

$$\begin{align*}n&=9+15+32+38+22+13+7\\n&=136\\M_p&=\frac{136+1}{2}\\M_p&=68.5\end{align*}$$

Use the 68th and 69th observations. The cumulative frequency is $56$ through score $-1$ and $94$ through score $0$, so both middle observations are $0$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{0+0}{2}\\\text{Median}&=0\end{align*}$$

answer.short: $35$, the mean of the 27th and 28th scores, $30$ and $40$.
answer.worked:
Cumulative frequencies: $14,22,27,35,41,44,54$.

$$\begin{align*}n&=14+8+5+8+6+3+10\\n&=54\\M_p&=\frac{54+1}{2}\\M_p&=27.5\end{align*}$$

Use the 27th and 28th observations. Cumulative frequency reaches $27$ at score $30$ and $35$ at score $40$, so the middle observations are $30$ and $40$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{30+40}{2}\\\text{Median}&=35\end{align*}$$
